```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
```

## Read my final data

```{r}
my_final_data <- read.csv("./data/processed/final_data.csv")
```

## Create coding-agent final data

```{r}
# Mortality data
matmor <- read.csv("./data/raw/maternal_mortality.csv")
infmor <- read.csv("./data/raw/infant_mortality.csv")
neomor <- read.csv("./data/raw/neonatal_mortality.csv")
un5mor <- read.csv("./data/raw/under5_mortality.csv")

mortality_fun <- function(data, varname) {
  data |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = starts_with("X"),
      names_to = "year",
      names_prefix = "X",
      values_to = varname
    ) |>
    mutate(year = as.numeric(year)) |>
    select(iso, year, all_of(varname))
}

matmor_long <- mortality_fun(matmor, "maternal_mortality")
infmor_long <- mortality_fun(infmor, "infant_mortality")
neomor_long <- mortality_fun(neomor, "neonatal_mortality")
un5mor_long <- mortality_fun(un5mor, "under5_mortality")
```

```{r}
# Disaster data
disaster <- read.csv("./data/raw/disaster.csv")

disaster_clean <- disaster |>
   janitor::clean_names() |>
  filter(
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2019,
    disaster_type %in% c("Earthquake", "Drought")
  ) |>
  select(year, iso, disaster_type) |>
  mutate(
    earthquake = if_else(disaster_type == "Earthquake", 1, 0),
    drought = if_else(disaster_type == "Drought", 1, 0)
  ) |>
  group_by(iso, year) |>
  summarise(
    earthquake = max(earthquake),
    drought = max(drought),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
# Conflict data
conflict <- read.csv("./data/raw/conflict.csv")

conflict_clean <- conflict |>
  mutate(
    armed_conflict = if_else(best >= 25, 1, 0)
  ) |>
  group_by(iso, year) |>
  summarise(
    armed_conflict = as.integer(max(armed_conflict)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(year + 1)
  )
```

```{r}
# Covariates
covariates <- read.csv("./data/raw/covariates.csv")
```

```{r}
# Coding-agent version of final data
agent_final_data <- list(
  matmor_long,
  infmor_long,
  neomor_long,
  un5mor_long,
  disaster_clean,
  conflict_clean,
  covariates
) |>
  reduce(full_join, by = c("iso", "year")) |>
  select(
    iso,
    year,
    armed_conflict,
    maternal_mortality,
    infant_mortality,
    under5_mortality,
    neonatal_mortality,
    drought,
    earthquake,
    gdp_1000,
    oecd,
    pop_dens,
    urban,
    age_dep,
    male_edu,
    temp,
    rainfall_1000
  )
```

## Standardize row order and variable types

```{r}
my_final_data_compare <- my_final_data |>
  arrange(iso, year) |>
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(year),
    drought = as.integer(drought),
    earthquake = as.integer(earthquake)
  ) |>
  as.data.frame()

agent_final_data_compare <- agent_final_data |>
  arrange(iso, year) |>
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(year),
    drought = as.integer(drought),
    earthquake = as.integer(earthquake)
  ) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

## Check whether the data sets are identical

```{r}
all.equal(
  my_final_data_compare,
  agent_final_data_compare
)
```

## Compare observations

```{r}
anti_join(
  my_final_data,
  agent_final_data,
  by = names(my_final_data)
)
```

```{r}
anti_join(
  agent_final_data,
  my_final_data,
  by = names(agent_final_data)
)
```

## Conclusion

The final data set created from my Week 3 code was compared with a second version independently recreated from the raw data.

Both data sets contained 3,732 observations and 17 variables, with the same variable names. Initial differences identified by `all.equal()` were due to row ordering and differences in variable classes. After sorting the observations and standardizing the variable types, `all.equal()` returned `TRUE`.

In addition, both `anti_join()` comparisons returned zero rows, indicating that there were no observations present in one data set but absent from the other.

Therefore, the final data set created from my Week 3 code and the data set independently recreated by the coding agent contain the same observations and values.
